subject: Stratus IoT: SLO qualification & ops playbook
messages:
From: Samir Kapadia <samir.kapadia@stratus-iot.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: priya.desai@stratus-iot.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Qualify: latency & streaming needs for Stratus IoT inference

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the intro and for taking time on the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size this correctly:

- Use case: on-device diagnostics and customer-facing anomaly summaries triggered by edge events. Short prompts (~20-80 tokens) with occasional longer follow-ups (~400 tokens).
- Expected peaks: roughly 120 concurrent sessions during morning sync windows; sustained baseline ~30 qps. Bursty bursts up to ~220 qps during firmware rollouts.
- Latency target: sub-150ms p95 for short prompts (customer-facing), streaming/partial response acceptable for long follow-ups but prefer <300ms chunk latency.
- Persistence: KV caching of recent device context (per-customer) would be useful.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the p95 numbers with streaming enabled, and what the main cost levers would be for us (e.g., batching, KV cache sizing, model quantization)? I attached our initial POC requirements and a sample network trace.

Attachments: stratus_poc_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-latency-traces.csv (csv)

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform, Stratus IoT
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Samir Kapadia <samir.kapadia@stratus-iot.com>
Cc: priya.desai@stratus-iot.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Qualify: latency & streaming needs for Stratus IoT inference

Hi Samir / Priya —

Great to meet earlier. Appreciate the detailed POC attachments — useful signal. Below is a concise post-call recap and proposed ops playbook so we can align on a target SLO and the engineering tasks to get you there.

Call recap / target SLOs (proposed):
- Short prompts (~20–80 tokens): target 100ms p95 (we can start at 150ms p95 to be conservative and tighten).
- Long follow-ups (streaming): aim for 200ms chunk latency, 95th percentile; end-to-end completion latency target 600ms p95 for typical 400-token requests with streaming.
- Concurrency/throughput: design for sustained 40 QPS, with burst capacity to 220 QPS using autoscale and reserved burst pool.

Primary cost/performance levers we recommend exploring in the POC:
1) Continuous batching and dynamic batch sizing — reduces per-token compute while preserving tail latency for short requests.
2) Prefix/KV caching — cache the device context per-customer with a small TTL (30–120s) to avoid recomputing repeated context across requests.
3) Quantization profiles — evaluate 8-bit quantization for the primary model; keep a higher-precision variant for fallbacks on critical requests.
4) Model variants and routing — route short, high-QPS traffic to a trimmed model variant (lower memory, faster kernels); route complex requests to the higher-capacity variant.
5) Streaming optimizations — aggressive early-token dispatch and small fixed chunk sizes to keep chunk latency predictable.

Action items / next steps:
- We will run a small benchmark using your provided traces against two quantized variants and one full-fp16 variant.
- Please confirm expected token distributions per request (average tokens in short vs. long flows).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive: propose Wed Feb 11 09:00 PT — 30m. We’ll include Ben (runtime), Aditya (kernel/quant), and Marissa (perf validation).

I attached our Redwood SLO playbook PDF that lays out configuration knobs and recommended thresholds. After the benchmark we’ll provide a recommended config (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quant profile) with expected cost delta.

Attachments: redwood-slo-playbook.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Stratus IoT: SLO qualification & ops playbook — ops plan request

Team — forwarding the Stratus POC details and my recap. Quick ask: can we assemble a short ops playbook that covers the POC config and who owns each step? I sketched owners inline below. Goal: have a runnable config and benchmark by EOD Feb 18 so the customer can validate in their staging window.

Owners / proposed tasks:
- Ben Carter (runtime): experiment with continuous batching + dynamic batch policy. Baseline: target batch window 8–12ms for short flows, max batch 256 tokens. Run with both gpt-medium-quant and gpt-small-quant variants.
- Aditya Rao (quant/kernel): provide two quant profiles (8-bit int8, q4_0-ish) and ensure kernels selected for short-seq optimized attention. Measure quality delta on 200 random prompts from their trace.
- Marissa Cole (eval/perf): run trace-driven benchmark (sustained 40 QPS + burst to 220 QPS). Record p50/p95/p99 for chunk latency and end-to-end completion. Validate caching hits with simulated KV TTLs 30s/60s/120s.

Technical notes to try in POC:
- Cache key format should be per-customer-device id; cache hit rate target >35% for short sessions to materially reduce cost.
- Fallback policy: if quantized variant misses quality threshold (>2% rouge/loss regression vs fp16 on eval set), route to fp16 for that request and send a telemetry event (metric: quant_fallback_rate).
- Autoscale policy: reserve a small burst pool (10% of expected capacity) to handle rollout spikes; pre-warm models for expected rollout windows.

Deliverables by Feb 18: benchmark CSV, recommended config file (json), and a short exec summary for the Stratus technical stakeholder.

Attachments included in thread: stratus_poc_requirements.xlsx, network-latency-traces.csv, redwood-slo-playbook.pdf

Thanks — please reply with concerns or confirm owners.

— Lauren
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Stratus IoT: SLO qualification & ops playbook — ops plan request

Lauren —

Looks good. I’ll start the batching experiments today and spin up the two quant variants Aditya prepares. Quick notes:
- I suggest we cap the dynamic batch latency to 12ms for the short-path service and prefer smaller fixed chunk sizes for streaming to stabilize chunk p95.
- I’ll instrument quant_fallback_rate + chunk_latency_p95 and share an early dashboard link by EOD Mon.

I’ll block time for the Wed deep-dive and will bring an initial benchmarking script.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
